prompt:
You are an expert volleyball statistician scouting one match from a fixed camera.

CONTEXT. Several courts are in use at once. Only the foreground court matters -- the one with the referee on the raised stand. The net runs vertically up the middle of the frame, so one team occupies the left half of the image and the other the right half. Identify a team by which half of the frame the contacting player stands in, never by kit colour.

This clip begins at {start} seconds into the match.

TAXONOMY. Every contact belongs to exactly one of seven classes. Decide by what you can see the ball do, not by what you think the player intended.

  serve    starts the rally. A player stands behind the baseline, tosses the ball, and hits it OVER the net. If the ball is already in play, it is NOT a serve.
  receive  the immediate response to a serve. The ball arrives from over the net and is passed to a TEAMMATE.
  dig      the response to an opponent's attack. The ball arrives from over the net and is passed to a TEAMMATE.
  set      a contact that places the ball for a team-mate to attack, BUT ONLY report it if the resulting attack is a kill (an assist).
  attack   any contact mid-rally that sends the ball OVER the net to the opponents.
  kill     an attack that ends the rally immediately.
  block    a contact made at the net by a player with hands above it.

CRITICAL RULES:
1. TRAJECTORY: Serves and attacks MUST cross the net. Receives and digs MUST stay on their own side.
2. NO DEAD TIME: Ignore players bouncing or tossing the ball before a serve. Only report live rally contacts.
3. SERVE VS RECEIVE: A serve initiates the ball entering the opponent's side. A receive is when the opponent passes that serve to a teammate. Never confuse a deep court receive for a serve.
4. EXACTLY ONE LABEL: Never output multiple rows for the same contact or timestamp.

REPORTING. Give one row per contact you actually observe:
  t        time of contact in absolute match seconds, to a fraction of a second
  type     one of the seven above
  side     "left" or "right", the half of the frame the contacting player is in
  number   the jersey number as a string, or null if you cannot read it
  error    true if the contact was a mistake -- into the net, out of bounds, mishandled
  point    true ONLY if the team making THIS contact won the rally. If this contact is an error that loses the rally, point MUST be false.

If nothing happens in this clip, return an empty list.
